rektion: etw./jdn. (Akk.) verpassen; ugs.: jdm. etw. verpassen (eine Ohrfeige)
meaning_en: to miss (a train, a chance, a person)
definition_de: zu spät kommen, sodass etwas schon weg ist (den Zug verpassen); eine Gelegenheit nicht nutzen (eine Chance verpassen)
example_de: Weil sie verschlafen hatte, verpasste sie den Zug nur um wenige Sekunden.
example_en: Because she had overslept, she missed the train by just a few seconds.
visual_idea: Collocation 'den Zug verpassen': an out-of-breath woman on the platform stretches her arm toward a train whose doors are closed and already pulling away. Her messy hair and half-buttoned coat show 'verschlafen'. Video optional (train leaving).
image_prompt: a young woman with messy hair and a half-buttoned coat standing out of breath at the edge of a German train station platform, one arm stretched out toward a red regional train whose doors are already closed as it pulls away, blank dark windows and plain red train side, her face frustrated, early morning light
negative_prompt: text, letters, watermark, signature, caption, blurry, extra fingers, deformed hands, cluttered background, multiple panels
video_prompt: a young woman with messy hair runs onto a train platform just as the doors of a red regional train close, she stretches out her arm while the train slowly pulls away and leaves, then she drops her arm and sighs; static wide shot
